subject: Proposal: Auto-renew notice and wind-down fee mitigation (Nimbus Analytics)
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@nim-analytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@nim-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: MSA: proposed changes to renewal / termination handling

Marcus / Karthik —

Thanks for the sync earlier. Attached is a short redline (NIM-MSA-redline-20260712.docx) with three items we need clarified before procurement can move forward:

1) Auto-renew notice: we asked to shorten the renewal notice period to 30 days (current draft is 60). For a company of our size shorter lead times are critical to avoid over-commitment.

2) Termination for convenience: we need an explicit TFC right on the MSA for the first 12 months after signature with a 90-day wind-down that requires Redwood to provide migration assistance and transfer of cached artifacts. We propose a cap on termination-related fees at 6 months of committed spend.

3) Data & export assistance: if the contract terminates for convenience, Nimbus requires a defined export process and at least 30 days of priority support to complete exports.

We're attaching our redline and looking for confirmation on whether Redwood is willing to accept these items (or propose commercial tradeoffs). Time is tight — procurement would like a final position before Friday.

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of Procurement
Nimbus Analytics

Attachments: NIM-MSA-redline-20260712.docx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@nim-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA: proposed changes to renewal / termination handling

Olivia —

Appreciate the clear ask and the redline. Quick reply with our initial commercial position so legal has context:

- Auto-renew notice: company policy defaults to 60 days for hosted commitments to allow capacity planning, but for enterprise commitments we can move to 45 days with a written carveout in the order form. We can consider 30 days only if Nimbus accepts a commitment-level uplift (5–10%).

- Termination for convenience (TFC): Redwood is open to a TFC right on multi-year or annual committed deals, but we need a structured wind-down: 90 days of operational assistance is reasonable; however, we're proposing the cap at 3 months of committed spend (not 6). That cap reflects expected provisioning and ramp costs.

- Data export & migration: we can commit to a documented export plan plus 30 days of prioritized support. For a longer wind-down we can offer tooling assistance and a single one-time transition credit (equivalent of 1 month of base committed fees).

I'm looping in Kimberly from Legal to convert the commercial points into redline language and confirm the implications for SLA/retention clauses. Karthik — FYI on the uplift incentive option if Nimbus prefers the 30-day renewal window.

Short attachment: marcus-summary-notes.txt (inline).

Next steps: Kimberly to propose MSA language / annex. If Nimbus can accept 45 days and the 3-month cap we can escalate to procurement for standard order form signoff.

Thanks,
Marcus
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia@nim-analytics.com>, LegalOps <legalops@nim-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA: proposed changes to renewal / termination handling

Folks —

I've reviewed Olivia's redline and Marcus's summary. High-level legal view and proposed language options attached (termination-winddown-annex-draft.pdf):

1) Auto-renew: We prefer 60 days as default for hosted services. We can add an Order Form clause that shortens notice to 45 days for this specific deal (acceptable commercially). I do NOT recommend 30 days without commercial uplift — operationally it's risky for capacity-managed pools.

2) Termination for convenience (TFC) mechanics: I can draft a narrow TFC that: (a) is available after the initial 12-month minimum term; (b) requires 90 days' wind-down during which Redwood provides migration assistance and priority support; (c) limits termination fees to a defined termination liability equal to "the lesser of three (3) months of committed fees or actual demonstrable provisioning costs." That mirrors what Marcus suggested.

3) Data/export: We'll commit to a documented export runbook and 30 days of prioritized support. I recommend adding a clause that Redwood will retain customer data for 60 days post-termination to allow for orderly transfer (per our retention policy).

4) Migration credit: legal is comfortable with a single one-time "transition credit" equal to one (1) month of base committed fees as consideration for migration assistance.

Please confirm whether Nimbus can accept the three-month cap and the 45-day renewal notice (with an uplift discussion if they insist on 30). If they push for 6-months cap or 30-day notice, we should treat that as a commercial ask and route to pipeline discounts / committed uplift.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: termination-winddown-annex-draft.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@nim-analytics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA: proposed changes to renewal / termination handling

Olivia —

Thanks for the transparency. Commercial trade-off we can offer to bridge to your 30-day preference without exposing us operationally:

Option A (no uplift): Accept 45-day auto-renew notice + 90-day wind-down + 3-month termination cap + 1 month transition credit.

Option B (commitment uplift): Move to 30-day auto-renew notice if Nimbus increases committed capacity by at least 10% for the first 12 months (we can discuss exact TCV). In that case we can also consider reducing the termination cap to 2 months.

I recommend Option A as the faster path to close. Marcus — please proceed to update the order form if Nimbus accepts Option A and I'll sign off on commercial concessions.

Karthik
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@nim-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, LegalOps <legalops@nim-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA: proposed changes to renewal / termination handling

Thanks all — appreciate the clear options and the quick turnaround.

Nimbus would prefer to move fast on Option A. We accept: 45-day auto-renew notice, 90-day wind-down with migration assistance, a termination cap of three (3) months of committed spend, and a one-time transition credit equal to one month of committed fees. Our procurement team will prepare a short purchase order contingent on the updated MSA and order form language.

Next steps from our side: I'll send Procurement's PO template and a short punch list (procurement-punchlist.xlsx). From Redwood: final MSA redline and order form with the 45-day notice clause and termination annex. Can Kimberly / Marcus target EOD Wednesday for the consolidated redline?

Best,
Olivia
Head of Procurement
Nimbus Analytics
